detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Robustness of physical records emerges when environmental channels broadcast pointer states (Quantum Darwinism) and structure information into redundant, accessible packets (Spectrum Broadcast Structures). Accessibility is constrained by observer-specific thresholds, necessitating a distinction between internal (system-integrated) and external perspectives.
detail.reason: Synthesizing new evidence into the established notebook to formalize the role of observer-specific access in record robustness.

detail.title: Synthesis of Observer-Dependent Robustness in Quantum Records
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes updated frameworks for understanding record robustness. Evidence from Quantum Darwinism, Spectrum Broadcast Structures, and internal-external observer models demonstrates that objectivity is not a monolithic property but an emergent feature dependent on environmental redundancy and observer-specific aperture.
